heldOutFilms: Encounters at the End of the World
The Battle of the River Plate

families.label: Two people reach for each other across a line drawn by those with authority over them, and the bond is refused before it can be lived.
The party taken in to help or to guard turns the trust placed in them against the one who placed it.
One party seizes what another loves and uses it to force them to give up their own side.
The one who did it goes free while another is made to carry the punishment for it.
An obligation made by people now gone still holds those who never agreed to it.
One party takes another's ruin onto themselves so the other does not have to bear it.
One party conceals another from those who would destroy them, and is endangered by the concealing.
One party enters closeness with another only for what can be taken out of it.
One party gives their word in exchange for something already handed over, then does not keep it.
A third person enters a bond of two and takes one of them away from the other.
One party looks on at what is most private to another, who cannot see the watcher or refuse the watching.
The pursuit changes the one doing the pursuing until the two have traded places.
One party goes and the other is left with no account of why, and has to live in the gap where the reason should be.
One party keeps faith with a bond the other is no longer there to hold.
One party comes asking of the one with the power to grant it, and is turned away without it.
The party nobody reckoned with turns out to be the one the outcome rests on.
One party hides their own condition from the people closest to them and keeps up the appearance that closeness requires.
The punishment owed for a deed is taken by someone other than the one who did it, while the one who did it stays free.
One party knows something that would ruin another, and by knowing it becomes the thing that other must remove.
One party knows of a wrong done and holds it unspoken, so the wrong goes on standing.
What one party made to serve them refuses the purpose it was given and turns back on the one who made it.
One party takes on the appetites of the one set above them and carries them further than the original ever did.
One party enters another's life carrying a purpose the other cannot see, and the closeness that grows between them is real anyway.
A group judges that someone within its reach is dangerous or has crossed a line, and turns its collective weight against them.
One party keeps giving to a bond the other has stopped returning, or never returned at all.
Two parties hold a claim on the same person, and the later claim can only be pressed at the cost of the earlier one.
One party takes what the other has not freely given, using the hold they already have over them.
One party's word is not credited by the very person bound to credit it.
One party acts on a picture of things that is wrong, and the truth reaches them only once the damage is done.
The party bound to shield another withdraws, or hands them over, at the moment the shielding is needed.
Someone who left returns to the people who let them go, and those who stayed have to decide what to do with them.
One party holds a bond in place by keeping something from the other that would change what the bond is.
One party lets fall the part they have been playing, and the other must re-read as performance what they took as real.
roles: the one who took it for real

families.label: One party settles what another is before that other has been allowed to answer.
One party knows what is true and cannot make it count with the party who would have to act on it.
roles: the one who cannot be credited
the one who will not credit them

families.label: One party keeps hold of a person so that what someone else values can be extracted from them.
One party decides what harm will be done and another party's hands or body carry it.
One party walks out of the bond and the other is left still standing inside it.
One party reaches for another who is already passing out of their hold, and the reach arrives after the moment for it.
One party discovers that the place they occupied in another's life can be filled by someone else.
roles: the one who fills the place
the one whose place it was

families.label: One party controls whether another may stay where they live, and the other must plead or qualify for the ground under them.
roles: the one who grants or withdraws
the one who must be allowed

families.label: One party settles an old injury on another, and the settling becomes the next injury to be settled.
roles: the one it is collected from

families.label: A child belongs to one party by blood and to another by raising, and both press the claim.
One party accepts their own death so the others may go on, and the others must live holding it.
roles: the one who stays to die

families.label: Two people can neither make the bond into what it might be nor get free of it.
roles: the one who will not let it close
the one who cannot leave it

families.label: A rupture between two people forces everyone around them to declare where they stand.
roles: those made to take a side

families.label: What becomes of one party's life is settled by another, and the one whose life it is has no standing in the decision.
What one party's life was is held by other people, and that party can only be told it.
roles: the one who holds the account
the one whose life it is

families.label: One party comes to see their own part in what passed between them only after the moment has closed on it.
roles: the one who comes to see
the one it was done to

families.label: One party unloads what has been done to them onto someone with less standing to refuse it.
A loss that no one can be shown to have caused is converted into blame settled on whoever can be reached.
One party comes to know or say the thing that must not be known, and the others move to shut them up.
One party withholds a fact that would alter what the other is standing in, and the other goes on standing in it.
One party keeps up a closeness whose real purpose is hidden from the other, who takes it for the thing itself.
One party arrives to occupy a place that belongs to another, and the displaced one has no claim left to make.
One party with no stake in a quarrel is made to enter it and take a side.
One party keeps up a relation with someone who can no longer answer for their own part in it, and so holds both sides alone.
One party's need to go on living puts their consent within reach of someone who can supply it.
One party's act is paid for by people singled out only for their tie to them.
One party is held guilty of a betrayal by the people closest to them, on grounds that settle nothing either way.
One party holds out a life the other can have only by ceasing to be who they were.
One party's readiness to turn on the others sets the terms under which everyone else has to live.
One party denies another what that other took to be their due, and the denied answers by destroying them.
One party is admitted to see a life shared by others but not to join it, and has to keep watching.
One party holds open an escape from what is closing in, and the other refuses it in order to stay with what binds them.
One party leaves a settled bond for someone newly arrived, and the one left is given no account they can live with.
One party treats another's life as a thing that can be owned, handed on, or bought back at a price.
One party comes back to someone they have carried in memory and meets a person who is no longer that.
One party orders their whole life around someone who is not there, either going after them or waiting on a promised return.
One party who cannot have the standing another holds turns on the person holding it.
A deed is fastened to a person in front of others, and the naming rather than the act decides what becomes of them.
One party acts to save another, and the act of saving is what ruins the one saved.
An older party's conviction governs a younger party's life, and the younger one has no standing to refuse it.
One party is fixed as the figure the people around them require, and can only take that name or refuse it.
A circle of people draws its life from a single person, and that person is cut off from ordinary relation with any of them.
One party courts another to reach something the courted one merely holds.
One party builds the whole bond out of looking, and the watched one is shaped by the look instead of being met.
One party is the source of both the care and the injury, and the other receives the injury as part of the love.
One party makes affection wait on a proof of worth, and the other keeps trying to satisfy the condition.
One party could sustain another who is failing and does not, and the one left goes under with no recourse.
An old injury is finally answered — repaid, confessed or repented — long after the moment when the answer could have changed anything.
One party puts themselves in the way of harm meant for another and pays what the other would have paid.
One party treats another's body or intimacy as purchasable, and the other is made to live inside that price.
One party holds another inside a bond, and every attempt to get out only fastens it tighter.
One party is taken in on trust and uses the inside position for ends belonging to someone else.
One party discharges a loss onto someone who did not cause it, and the other must absorb what they did not do.
One party is taken for what they are not, and the mistake decides how they are treated until it breaks.
One party holds back the thing the other most needs to know, and keeping it back becomes work of its own.
One party can only stay alive by doing to another the thing they would have condemned.
Two who depend on each other each come to expect the worst of the other, and the dependence turns hostile.
One party makes another the hands that carry out a cruelty the other party decided on.
One party carries knowledge of a danger to the people who could act on it, and they will not take it.
One party sets the terms on which another may speak of what happened to them, and no true account fits those terms.
A penalty meant for one person lands on another who stands where they stood.
A household opens itself to someone on trust and that person uses the place inside it to feed on them.
Someone under no obligation takes in a person and gives them the care they are owed by others who withhold it.
A child is given over to be raised by someone outside the family that bore them.
One party has settled the shape of another's life in advance, and the other had no part in the settling.
A body of people treats one of their number as the life to be given up so the rest may continue.
Someone who is gone leaves an unfinished obligation and the living take it onto themselves.
One party puts themselves forward for admission while the other holds all the power to take them in or pass them over.
A judgment falls against the weaker party, and being in the right does not protect them.
One party wants someone already bound to another, and that existing bond is the whole of the obstacle.
One party keeps care over a body that can no longer answer or act for itself.
One party values another strictly for what that party supplies, and drops or turns on them the moment the supply ends.
One party fixes another's standing with a charge or a fact, and nothing the marked party can say or do removes it.
The party charged with finding who is to blame is the party that holds the blame, and hands it to someone who cannot carry it back.
One party is playing a part in a relation the other is living for real, and the relation lasts only as long as the part holds.
Everyone around a person holds the fact that bears on them most, and agrees among themselves that the person will not be given it.
One party requires a lethal act of another and stays out of the doing, so the whole weight of it falls on the hands that were sent.
One party loads a life's aim of their own onto someone bound to them, who must live it out in place of a purpose of their own.
Whether two people may join is settled by parties standing outside the bond, and the ones inside it have no standing to answer.
One party goes and the other keeps the bond in place alone, so that waiting becomes their entire share of it.
Two parties who belong to each other come to want the same thing, and the claim can only be settled by one of them unmaking the other.
A party in need is held and carried by people who owe them nothing, in the place of those who owed it and withdrew.
One party with means wears away another's hold on what they live from, by pressure over time rather than by seizing it.
One party refuses to concede what everyone around them treats as already settled, and their agreement is exactly what cannot move them.
One party departs for reasons of their own and the other is left in the place they shared, with no standing to follow or refuse.
One party takes the service, loyalty or labour they were given and drops the giver once it is no longer needed.
One party stands beside the other as a trusted intimate while acting for the side that means them harm.
The lie is broken open in front of the very person it was built for, and the two must go on facing each other after.
One party lets the charge settle on someone who did not do it, because the truth would cost them more.
One party gives a true account of themselves and the other refuses to take it, so they are treated as the thing they say they are not.
One party sees plainly what is being done to the other and neither moves nor names it, so the watching becomes part of the harm.
One party can say what happened only by ruining themselves, so what was done to the other stays unsaid.
One party takes a person out of the hands of those bound to them, and the loss becomes the whole of what those left must do.
One party's life narrows entirely to finding the other, until the looking has cost more than the finding could return.
One party is set to run the other down while bound to them by something the chase cannot account for, so ending it would end them both.
The injury comes from the hand that was supposed to keep the other safe, and is done in the name of keeping them.
One party uses the other's duty to obey them as the instrument of what is done to them.
A death is set up beforehand as an arrangement between parties, so that when it comes it is the keeping of an agreement.
One party holds a tie to someone outside the couple, and the bond survives only for as long as that tie goes unnamed.
One party wants a child their own life will not give them, and must put that want onto another person to answer.
One party must be taken for someone they are not in order to be tolerated, and every exchange with the other rests on that.
What one party finally admits reaches a listener it was never meant for, and the wrong hearing changes both of them.
One party comes back to a person or place they left, and is met by something that no longer answers to the memory they returned for.
One party in need calls on those bound to answer for them, and the call is heard and not taken up.
One party, having been damaged, delivers the same damage to someone who had no part in it.
One party settles the other's life for them on the strength of family alone, and the other is given no standing to refuse.
One party enters or grants closeness in order to use the other, while the other takes the bond as real.
One party has another carry out the work or the harm that belongs to the one directing it.
The dying or the dead lay an obligation on someone still living, and the living party cannot put it down.
One party takes over what another built and is known for it, while the one who made it is unnamed.
One party withholds from another a fact about that person's own beginning, and its surfacing undoes who they took themselves to be.
A child is claimed both by those who raised him and by those he came from, and being kept by one is a loss to the other.
One party holds knowledge that would ruin another, and the holding of it is what puts them in danger.
A wrong is known to everyone including the one who did it, and no one can be made to answer for it.
A past suffering is staged again in front of watchers, and the playing of it works on the performer as the memory alone did not.
One party offers closeness and the other will not have it, and the refusal is not something the wanting can work on.
A third person's presence turns a bond into something the two must contest rather than hold.
One party keeps to a commitment for the sake of the bond alone, not for the thing committed to.
A person's loss is met by someone with no prior claim on them, who reaches them where their own could not.
One party holds knowledge that belongs to another and does not hand it over, and the not-telling becomes its own act between them.
One party holds a person and will let them go only for what the holder names as owed.
roles: the one whose release is priced

families.label: One party has the standing to dispose of another's life and uses it, and the other's consent is never required.
One party holds the power to allow a bond between others and refuses it, and the bond cannot proceed without them.
A newcomer takes the place another held in someone's attachment, and the first is set aside without having done anything wrong.
roles: the one who takes the place

families.label: One party sustains a false version of themselves before another and it comes apart in that other's hands.
roles: the one who shows a false face
the one it is shown to

families.label: One party is trusted to speak or act on another's behalf while actually serving a different interest.
roles: the one who acts in another's name
the one who relies on them

families.label: One party holds knowledge about another that can destroy them, and everything between them turns on what is done with it.
One party is bound to a cause or an order and sets aside what they owe the person in front of them.
roles: the one bound to the larger claim
the one set aside for it

families.label: One party can only go on while another chooses to stay or to keep holding them, and that choice is not theirs.
A settled group decides whether an unvouched newcomer is taken in or kept suspect, and admission is theirs alone to grant.
roles: the ones who hold the threshold
the one seeking to be let in

families.label: One party controls what standing is granted and withholds from another the recognition their service or loss has earned.
What one side does to the other is returned to them, and the positions swap rather than settle.
Two parties who stand against each other are held together with no way out and must finally reckon with one another.
What happened between the parties survives only as accounts that cannot be reconciled, and whoever must carry one cannot vouch for it.
roles: the one who must take it on trust

families.label: One party lays a wrong before the person it harmed, and what happens next is entirely the harmed party's to decide.
roles: the one who admits the wrong
the one who must answer it

families.label: One party takes up a role toward the other that the tie between them never called for, and the bond is re-set on that footing.
roles: the one who offers new terms
the one who must accept them

families.label: One party leaves or is driven from the shared home, and everything rests on whether the other comes after them.
One party presses for a bond the other has already ended or given elsewhere, and asks for what is no longer theirs to have.
roles: the one who has closed it

families.label: One party comes back to people who have arranged their lives around their absence, and the place they left has been filled.
One party takes or claims a person out of the hands of those who hold them, and both sides assert a right to the same person.
One party is made to answer for a wrong another committed, and the one who did it stays unnamed.
The harm comes from the party who was given charge, taken in or set loose, not from outside.
One party says plainly what is true or needed and the other cannot or will not receive it, and the cost falls where the speaker said it would.
One party settles on another's guilt and acts on it, holding neither evidence nor any standing to judge.
One party holds something the other cannot afford to lose and makes them pay for it, and paying once does not end it.
One party hands over the person bound to them, using the closeness itself as the means.
What one party kept hidden about where they came from is uncovered by the other, and the bond cannot stand on the old terms.
One party's living, comfort or amusement is drawn directly from another party's ruin.
One party destroys people so that a position or a story of its own can go on standing.
A third person's desire enters a bond already formed, and the arrangement cannot hold all three.
One party accepts their own ruin as the price of another's keeping, and the other cannot refuse it.
A dependent is held and raised by people who are not their own and who keep them for their own reasons.
The party with the power to grant someone a place withdraws it, and the other has no standing left to appeal with.
One party sustains or repays another while keeping the source hidden, so the good done is credited elsewhere or to no one.
One party withholds their own history or work from the person closest to them, believing the bond cannot survive the telling.
A bond exists that one party requires be lived as though it does not, and the other holds to that requirement.
One party has ended the bond and the other will not accept that it is ended.
One party is owed return or rescue by the person bound to give it, and that person does not come.
The party charged with keeping another safe is the one through whom the harm arrives.
A consequence that belongs to one party falls on another, who bears it in their place while the first goes free.
One party's ability to leave is in someone else's keeping, and its price is set by them.
A group shuts itself against a single person whose terms are not theirs, and the person will not adopt the group's terms.
One party arranges what others are living through from a position the others cannot see, so they act on a situation someone made for them.
The person admitted closest to another's work or authority is the one who sells them out.
What one party knows makes them something another must silence, and the knowing itself is the danger.
The authority a party has served violates or withdraws the terms it set, leaving the one who kept faith with nothing to have kept faith with.
One party fixes the account of what happened or of who someone is, and the party it concerns cannot contest it.
One party forces or presses another into a physical or binding tie the other did not choose, and the other must go on living inside it.
One party treats their regard as something that must be paid for or proved, and the other keeps performing for a love that is never simply given.
One party accepts help or gives loyal service without knowing what the other means to take from them for it.
One party holds another in place by a claim — a debt, a price, an affection — that the other can neither discharge nor refuse.
One party is filled in for or dropped the moment they are gone or no longer useful, revealing they were held for a function and not for themselves.
One party arranges a way out and the other will not take it, choosing the ruin they are in over the deliverance offered.
One party is dead or dying and the other goes on living under their instruction, carrying work or restraint that cannot be argued with.
One party requires an act or a handover from another who depends on nothing but their compliance, and that other quietly does not deliver it.
One party puts their need onto someone with no stake in it, and that passerby must decide whether to take up a burden that is not theirs.
One party holds a truth that would cost another their standing, and that other moves to unsay it or to remove the one who holds it.
One party fixes a name or a verdict on another, and the other's life turns on refusing it or disproving it.
One party has without effort what the other cannot reach at any cost, and the watching becomes unbearable.
One party carries a debt or an attachment toward another that can never be spoken to them, and the other never learns it was owed.
One party moves to take a child out of the keeping of another, and where the child belongs is settled between them rather than by the child.
One party observes another from a position the other cannot see, and the watching changes the life it was meant only to record.
One party settles another person's future into a bond that person did not choose and is in no position to refuse.
People with no claim on one another take up the duties of kin toward each other anyway.
One party goes and does not return, and the other has to keep living in the shape of that absence.
One party comes to claim their place in a bond and finds someone else standing in it.
One party keeps from another a truth that belongs to that other, and calls the keeping protection.
One party sets the terms of a pursuit and ends up the one caught by the terms they set.
One party turns another's need or attachment into a tool for an end that is not the other's own.
A community takes hold of conduct one party held to be their own affair and judges it openly.
One party keeps back what the other is owed, knowing the other has no way to make them give it.
Two parties answer each other past the original grievance until the answering itself decides the outcome.
One party grants help or clemency they were not supposed to grant, to someone who cannot repay it.
One party holds another somewhere no outside authority reaches, and answers to nobody for what is done there.
Two parties go on with each other in the interval between a harm becoming certain and its arrival.
roles: the one the harm is coming for
the one who stays beside them

families.label: The one holding a place comes to fear the younger party who stands to take it.
One party holds to another only while the bond serves them, and lets them go the moment it starts costing something.
One party gives service or help and is answered with hatred or violence by the very people it was given to.
One party keeps another within reach by force, so that leaving is no longer the other's to decide.
A prior tie is honoured over a wanted love or life, and whoever wanted it is forsaken by that choice.
A newcomer takes the place one party held in another's affection, and the displaced one is simply passed over.
One party knows what would undo another, and the other's life rests on whether it is spoken.
One party is put back inside the thing they escaped, by someone else's arrangement.
One party moves among people who trust them wearing a face that is not theirs, and it is the trust itself that opens the way to the harm.
One party presses another into the shape of a person who is gone, and asks them to be someone they are not.
An older party sets the terms on which a younger one may live, and the younger must break them or be bound by them.
One party is named as the guilty one and the naming holds, whatever the accused says or does not say.
One party holds another in their charge and uses that hold against them, so the harm comes from the very hand that was meant to keep them.
One party pursues another as quarry, and the chase becomes the whole of what passes between them.
Harm falls on one party and no one with the standing to answer for it will own it as theirs.
What would settle the matter rests with a party who cannot deliver it, so it falls to someone else to speak for them or to no one at all.
roles: one who would speak or hear

families.label: One party may keep a place among others only by surrendering something of their own, and must decide which of the two to lose.
One party settles an injury by inflicting it back, and the settling becomes the next injury.
One party stands as parent to a child they hold no secured right to, and must earn the place or live with having forfeited it.
One party's standing in the bond rests entirely on a choice that the other alone is permitted to make.
One party is given charge of another's safety or keeping and uses that position to take from them instead.
One party manages what another is allowed to believe about their own life, and the other lives inside the version they are given.
A person is taken by others for the reverse of what they are, and nothing they do reads as evidence against the reading.
One party keeps another alive and the rescue itself becomes a tie neither of them chose.
The only help on offer comes from someone who gives it in order to acquire a hold over the one who takes it.
A body of power keeps itself clean by letting the person who acted for it carry the consequence alone.
A person is put out of the life they belonged to by people who have decided they are no longer worth keeping.
A person arranges their whole existence around a single act they believe they committed against another.
Someone goes back to mend a bond they left and finds the moment when mending was possible has passed.
A person owes two parties at once and cannot answer one without wounding the other.
A person conceals the life they actually live in order to pass among people who would not accept it.
A child sees what the parent actually is and can no longer be held by the figure the parent was.
A person has nothing to trade but themselves and spends that to buy what cannot otherwise be got.
One person takes damage onto themselves to hold up another who cannot stand alone.
Two people are held to each other by a bond they are not permitted to live out.
One person spends themselves looking for another who has gone, without knowing whether there is anyone left to find.
One party sends a child out of the household, and the bond is broken by the sending rather than by anything either party wanted.
The party who cheated another returns into their life and the harm between them is undone.
One party finds that the person they relied on had been working against them all along.
One party carries a fear to the people nearest them and those people decline to take it seriously.
One party stays in the other's company while no longer receiving anything the other says.
One party is already given to someone when their attachment settles on another.
One party surrenders what they most want, or their life, so that a member of their family is spared.
A matter is settled between two parties and the price of the settlement is paid by someone who had no part in it.
One party holds the disposal of another's life and labour and will not hand it back when asked for.
The matter goes to whichever party is stronger rather than to whichever party has the claim.
One party strips another of standing, and the stripping is answered not by argument or apology but by a death.
One party finally puts to another a truth about their family they have held for a very long time, and the bond has to take it.
The party someone depends on for protection is secretly the source of the harm, and the one depending does not know.
One party takes what another has to give and puts them aside once they have given it.
One party offers to close the distance and the other refuses the offer outright.
A third party decides whom someone may love, and their attachment is disposed of for that party's ends.
Two parties claim the same person entirely, and the person's turning toward one unmakes the other.
The one who raised and the one raised are separated by a departure that cannot be taken back.
One party's wrong goes unanswered because the one who would call them to account cannot.
One party is obliged to work for or alongside someone they are set against, and the enmity does not go away.
One who was once helped returns to the one who helped them, and what they hand back settles what the bond was.
The one who taught dies and leaves the unfinished work in the hands of the one taught.
One party forms another into a figure of their own wanting and holds the result as theirs to keep.
One party will not hold their ground, and someone else pays what that costs.
One party comes back from being counted gone and finds the life they left has closed over the gap they made.
One party holds another only for as long as that other is of use, and sets them aside when the use runs out.
One party knows the true account of another's life and acts on it while keeping that other inside a false one.
The one who made or taught another is overtaken by what he made, and the making turns back on him.
The one who brought another into being refuses the thing that being asks of him.
One party holds another's destruction in hand and chooses instead who will be spared.
One party can only get what they need by flattering someone who holds power over them, and their standing turns on whether they will stoop to it.
One party holds another to account for a wrong they have themselves committed and concealed.
One party owes something to those they harmed or failed to save that no act of theirs can discharge.
A private matter is dragged before onlookers who pass judgement on it, and the person it belongs to carries the cost.
One party takes in and raises someone they did not beget, and the bond has no claim behind it to hold it in place.
One party is trusted from the inside while acting for an interest the other party does not know about, and every intimacy becomes a channel for that other interest.
What one party extended to another — shelter, teaching, a life — comes back as the instrument of that party's ruin, in the hands of the one who received it.
A group secures its own cohesion by turning on a single member, and the one singled out cannot answer it as an equal.
A party's fate is settled by others who never put the question to the party it concerns.
One party controls what another is permitted to know and acts to stop the truth from reaching the person it concerns.
One party gives help for a reason the receiver is never told, so the help binds the receiver to terms they cannot see.
Two parties press a claim on the same person, who cannot be divided or shared between them.
A debt is enforced through a substitute, one party collecting or answering for someone who is not there to do it.
One party's living is drawn directly from another party's misfortune, so relief for the one means loss for the other.
The danger to someone arrives through the very person bound to keep them safe, and the bond is what makes it unstoppable.
Something a person set in motion comes back and destroys the person who set it in motion.
roles: the one who set it in motion

families.label: One person moves among others who take him for someone else, and everything that follows rests on their error.
A gathered public, party to nothing, confers the verdict that settles what an act meant and what becomes of the one who did it.
A judgment is fixed before it is heard, and the person condemned is chosen for convenience rather than for what they did.
One party holds out a way to survive or settle, and the other refuses it and pays for refusing.
roles: the one who offers a way out

families.label: An obligation owed to the dead outranks what the living need, and the one who carries it cannot set it down.
The line dividing two sides runs straight through a bond, so that belonging to one side means betraying someone loved on the other.
roles: the one who belongs to both
the side that demands the whole of them

families.label: A binding promise between two people is undone by a feeling that arrives after it was made.
roles: the one who breaks the pledge

families.label: A person turns away from the love that is actually available to them and can only want it at a distance.
One person knows plainly what is true and can get no one else to credit it, so the knowledge buys no power to act.
roles: the ones who will not credit it

families.label: Someone sent or showing something between parties is made to answer for its content as though it were their own doing.
roles: the one who receives it badly

families.label: A person discovers they were weighed against something else and were not the one chosen.
Someone comes back to a bond after an absence and learns whether it held a place for them or closed over.
One party comes back to a bond they abandoned, and the other has been holding the place all along.
One party goes out from the shared life and the other stays inside it, and the bond has to survive the gap.
One party disposes of another person's future for their own benefit, and the person disposed of is not consulted.
One party's life is used as the material out of which another party's advancement is made.
One party remakes another into the figure they require until the person and the figure can no longer be told apart.
Two parties want the same person and one of them is put aside, and the setting aside is what the situation turns on.
Care passes between two parties who are placed on opposite sides of a standing hostility.
One party has taken more from another than was theirs, and nothing settles until it is handed back.
One party's true quality is received by everyone as its opposite, and nothing they say or do corrects it.
One party will not give the love another needs and does not give a reason the other can use.
One party's account is set aside in favour of another's, and nothing the disbelieved one can say will move it back.
The one word that would settle a charge is held back by the only party who can say it.
A newcomer is installed in a place another already holds, and the one displaced has no standing from which to object.
One party's scorn is answered by the other turning harm on themselves rather than on the one who scorned them.
One party keeps up an appearance they know to be false, and is given standing by the other precisely because of it.
One party's whole position exists at another's discretion, and is passed on or let go when that other chooses.
One party alone gets through to someone the rest had given up on, and thereafter that person reaches the world only through them.
One party returns after time has passed to make the other answer for a taking the other had treated as closed.
One party cannot make what they know count for anything against the account the other has already accepted.
The only party offering shelter or affection is the same party keeping the other from leaving.
One party carries a cost that belongs to another's stake, and the other is spared without having asked for it or being told.
A power neither party chose cuts the bond between them, and what the two of them want counts for nothing.
Others settle on a false account of who someone is, and life proceeds on that account as if it were the true one.
The thing that was to hold two people together never arrives or is lost, and the bond cannot stand on its own.
A community withholds standing from someone for what they are rather than anything they have done, and no conduct can earn it back.
One party is charged with a wrong in a form that leaves the other no way to answer it.
One party holds what the other cannot do without and names the terms on which it is returned.
One party can only secure themselves by laying the cost on someone who has done nothing to earn it.
One party's capacity has to serve for another's incapacity, and neither can act apart from the other.
One party ends a bond the other still holds, and the one who holds it is given no part in the decision.
One party keeps an intention across years without declaring it and moves only when the other can no longer withstand it.
One party's standing exists only at another's pleasure, and the one who raised them sets them aside without account.
People outside a bond claim authority over it and act against it, and the two in it must answer to a judgment they never invited.
One party holds another's safety or keep and turns that dependence into a demand the dependent cannot refuse without losing it.
The person who does the harming is the same person the harmed one is tied to, so the harm does not end the bond.
One party presses the other for something only freely given, and the other will not give it.
A wrong is answered for directly between the parties, with no institution standing behind the accounting.
One party extends help or consolation and the other refuses it, because accepting would mean conceding something they cannot concede.
